leverage.exposure: Negative balance, no offers placed, nothing at risk tonight. The deficit only bites at the instant the matchday locks, and that is still most of four days out. If both flips are won the exposure roughly triples for a day or so, and the unwind was checked end to end: selling both back after the tick, then Treu after Thursday's tick, clears the debt with room to spare and still leaves a legal eleven well before the lock. No action is needed on the exposure itself until the flips settle.

binding_gap: Defence, and specifically the hole that opens the moment Treu goes: Nakuzola is forced into the eleven and he is by some distance the weakest body you own. The money to fix it is thin. Selling Treu alone leaves only a sliver, and selling Nakuzola alongside him frees a little more but not much — and both figures were re-derived from live data this run because the ceilings carried in the ledger no longer reconcile and had their labels the wrong way round. At that budget the board holds one plausible defender and one who is plainly out of favour at his club. Flip profit would widen this, but flip profit belongs to the value trade and is deliberately not counted here.

verdict.headline: Quiet window.
verdict.detail: Quiet window. One new listing and one settled transfer in the whole two hours, and neither changes the plan. The instruction is exactly what the last run gave you: bid mv on the two open Kickbase flips, bid nothing else, and leave Treu alone until after the Thursday tick. Nothing needs you tonight.

sell.reason: Treu remains the one and only sale, and it is still a sale of timing rather than urgency. He is fit, news-clear and named in Freiburg's probable eleven against Schalke, which is exactly why he is worth more every day: he is rising, so the right move is to hold him through Thursday's tick and then instant-sell him back to Kickbase. He clears the deficit on his own and leaves a legal eleven, which no other single sale in the squad does. The cost is honest and should not be glossed: he is the lowest-scoring player in your fielded eleven, but Nakuzola, who replaces him, is far worse. No second sale is recommended — Gruber looks tempting as a faller, but selling him breaks the shape with nothing funded to replace him.

Selling him alone takes the balance to +875.973 with exactly 11 players, which satisfies both constraints with nothing to spare. THE CORRECTED DEADLINE IS THE LOCK ITSELF, NOT 06.10: the 06.10 date in S9cv1ds came from the expiry of a rival 13.500.000 manager ask that is no longer the comparator. DO NOT SELL HIM TONIGHT. He is mvt 1 with sdmvt +132.248 and tfhmvt +45.161, and three ticks remain before the lock (06.10, 07.10, 08.10 — the 09.10 20:00Z tick falls AFTER the 18:30Z lock and does not count). At the re-measured mvt-1 mean of +2,51% that compounds 12.944.013 to roughly 13.943.000, so waiting until 08.10 evening or the morning of 09.10 is worth about +1.000.000 over selling now. This supersedes and quantifies We5wpap, whose four-tick arithmetic counted one tick too many. THE KNOWN AND ACCEPTED COST: Treu carries ap 76 and is in the fielded eleven, so his sale forces Nakuzola (ap 27) in and the formation to a rigid 4-4-2 with zero slack — a loss of 49 ap. There is no cheaper unwind. The alternatives are worse: Gruber at 9.240.326 does not clear the deficit and he is the st-2 injury flag, and Deman at 9.077.827 likewise falls short. FITNESS: Treu is st 0, and the only Treu news found remains the SEPTEMBER DFB item already flagged as a date trap in Wk36xnt — no current info found newer than that. His sale is an unwind decision, not a fitness decision.

buy.reason: Nothing on the board clears the bar, and that is a real answer rather than a shrug. Every manager ask currently listed is priced far above market value, and the ones that are not are already killed in writing by an open avoid. The only new listing since the last run is a Kickbase board listing that belongs in the flip queue, not the points squad — you are already deep in midfielders and he would not reach your eleven. The one honest buy candidate is a cheap St. Pauli defender who would be a small upgrade on Nakuzola for almost no money, but his listing runs past tonight's tick, so his rising flag has to be re-read afterwards before anyone bids. That decision belongs to the first run after the tick, not to this one.

Two further strikes: the ask is ABOVE mv, and a manager ask above mv has never been a buy at any point in this ledger's history; and Georg already carries two Augsburg players (Gregoritsch, Wolf), so a third concentrates club risk in a side away at Bayern on MD5. REVERSAL: require ALL of (1) the ask at or BELOW mv, (2) a non-negative balance with genuine spare capacity above the floor, and (3) a marginal-points test against whoever he would actually displace AT THAT TIME, not against Tanaka's 87 as of today. Being the only sanely-priced ask on the board is NOT a reason to buy.

movers.reason: The flip queue is unchanged and still the best thing on the table. Both open flips are Kickbase board listings priced at exactly market value with a rising flag and, critically, both expire before tonight's tick, so winning either means owning him when the value updates. Bid market value exactly and never raise — chasing one of these into a contested clear destroys ten good flips at once. The new Werder listing qualifies on every leg and is genuinely good, but it does not fit alongside both of the others, so it is the substitute leg: bid it only if one of the first two is lost. A second wave of three qualifying listings runs past tonight's tick and is deliberately left alone until their flags can be re-read. The edge itself was re-measured this run and has not decayed — the sample has grown and both the average move and the hit rate are fractionally better than the baseline. The reason why showed up in the feed tonight: the league's most active trader bought a falling player at a premium, which is the exact inverse of the trade. Two questions remain open and unresolved — whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can run at once, and the standing caveat that this edge is measured in one league over one period and will decay if rivals ever do crowd in.

Treu is clean — the alarming headlines that rank top on a plain search are all last season's story and the traps held again. Engelhardt is confirmed in Freiburg's eleven, the first dated starter confirmation since his buy cleared.
